title: Benji and the Falling Seeds
markdown:
Benji watched Dapple prance after a butterfly. "Ms. Quill!" he called. "Why did Dapple’s apple core drift down so slowly, like a puff? But when I kicked a stone, zoom! It shot straight down! They’re both just… falling, aren’t they?" Dapple nodded, ears twitching.

Ms. Quill, whose eyes twinkled like stars, chuckled. "Ah, Benji, a truly excellent question! The world is full of puzzles. Come, let’s find out together."

They ambled over to a grassy hill. Ms. Quill took two sheets of paper. She creased one into a sharp dart, the other into a wide glider. Benji gathered small, dry seed pods.

"Ready?" Ms. Quill chirped from the crest. "One… two… three!"

The paper dart zipped down. The glider wobbled and dipped. Benji’s winged seed took its sweet time. The plain seed, however, dropped unceremoniously.

Benji’s brow furrowed. "It's like… the air is pushing back!" he whispered. He watched the glider drift.

"Precisely!" Ms. Quill beamed. "The air is all around us! When something falls, this invisible air tries to slow it down. The wider and flatter something is, the more air it bumps into. It’s like the air is giving it a gentle hug!"

Benji picked up a leaf. It caught the air and drifted. He grabbed a twig. It fell much faster. Suddenly, a gust lifted a feather, sending it twirling high above. "Look!" whinnied Dapple. "The feather dances!"

"That's because it catches so much air!" Ms. Quill explained. "It’s like a tiny parachute! That push from the air makes it float. It’s a beautiful dance between the falling object and the air!"

Suddenly, Benji’s eyes lit up. His friend Pip was growing giant sunflower seeds. Benji needed to deliver them, but the meadow could be windy. He worried the seeds might get lost.

"Ms. Quill," Benji asked, "if I make the seed packet wide and flat, like your glider, won't it just float away?"

"It might indeed," she agreed. "But if you make it pointed, like that sharp dart, it will cut through the air more easily. The wind won't have as much to grab onto."

Benji found bark and folded it into a neat, pointed packet. He placed the precious sunflower seeds inside. Dapple watched, ears perked.

"Ready, Dapple?" Benji grinned. Dapple nudged Benji’s hand. Benji took a deep breath, tossed the packet, and watched. It sailed across the meadow in a steady, straight line, landing gently at Pip’s garden gate.

"Hooray!" cheered Benji, hugging Dapple. "It worked! The seeds are safe!"

Ms. Quill smiled warmly. "And wouldn't you know it," she said softly, "that push from the air is what clever folks call air resistance. It's a curious thing, how shape can make things fall at different speeds. It's a secret game the air plays with everything."

Benji looked up at the sky, then at Dapple, then at Ms. Quill. He wondered what other secrets were hiding, just waiting to be discovered. And Dapple was already eyeing a dandelion.
characters: Benji the telescope helper, Dapple the pony, Ms. Quill
